acceptance.output_evidence: THREE ANSWERS, NO VERDICT. (a) THE WRITER IS THE RIGHT LAYER, AND WHAT MAKES THAT MORE THAN CONVENIENCE IS A MEASUREMENT: of the 3 counted writers of this key space, exactly ONE deletes by key; the other two replace the whole table and are structurally incapable of destroying a row they did not write. Had the census returned two filtered writers this answer would have INVERTED to the table's identity, because a per-writer fix on a shared seam is the per-member fix Rule 22 warns about. But the writer layer closes only ONE of the two defects here: the DESTRUCTION is closed, the AMBIGUITY is not -- opal-data-portal-v2 is still a string two classes both answer to, and reading this fix as 'the key collision is fixed' is wrong in a way that matters. (b) IT HAS ALREADY RECURRED, FOUR MORE TIMES, and the unscoped read found it while a scoped one would not have: IAM_ROLE+LAMBDA 8, EVENT_RULE+LAMBDA 8, CODEBUILD_PROJECT+IAM_ROLE 1, EVENT_RULE+SSM_DOCUMENT 1. These are NOT naming mistakes and must not be treated as ones -- a function and its execution role sharing a name is good practice. What is defective is a schema in which identity is a short name in one column and a full ARN in another with a rule that falls back between them; canonical_node_key already states the correct rule and the failure was that the delete predicate did not USE it. So the recurrence class is narrower and more actionable: every place that treats arn and node_id as ONE match space instead of applying the canonical rule. Three such places were found in one file; the estate was NOT censused for others, and that is a stated limit of this order's coverage rather than an absence. (c) CG-s-33 SHOULD STILL DEPLOY AND IS NOT REDUNDANT -- the two are halves of one identity problem and each leaves the other's failure standing. CG-s-33 fixes WHERE AN EDGE LANDS; this order fixes WHETHER A NODE SURVIVES. Deploy only CG-s-33 and the graph still silently loses nodes, and they are now nodes nothing points at, which is HARDER to notice. Deploy only this and the 27 SERVED_FROM edges keep landing on a bucket policy that is not what they mean. ONE ASYMMETRY IS FLAGGED FOR WHOEVER SEQUENCES: this fix is safe in either order, CG-s-33 is safer AFTER it, because re-pointing edges while the destroyer is live re-points onto a population still being thinned. That is named as a measured ordering property, not issued as a sequencing instruction, which is not a worker's act.
